title: Towns
subtitle: suburbs, outskirts, facilities, bustling
summary: Describe a town or city - its layout, its facilities, its problems - and choose the adjective that captures what it feels like.

lesson.heading: City or town?
lesson.text: The words **city** and **town** are sometimes used interchangeably, but a city is generally large with a wider range of **facilities**. Here is how a guidebook describes Cork, one of Ireland's main cities.

examples.text: Cork city is the major **metropolis** of the south; with a **population** of about 119,500, it is the second largest city in the Republic.
examples.note: a metropolis is a very large or important city

examples.text: The main business and shopping centre lies on the island created by two channels of the River Lee, with many of the **suburbs within walking distance** of the centre.
The buses tend to be **overcrowded** and the **one-way traffic system** is extremely complicated.
The fashionable **residential districts** of Cork **overlook** the picturesque harbour. There are other residential areas on the **outskirts**.
examples.note: the outskirts = the outer parts of a town, away from the centre

lesson.heading: Phrases a guidebook uses
lesson.text: These phrases come up again and again when someone describes a place. Learn them whole.

examples.text: St Anne's Church was built on the **site** of a church destroyed when the city was besieged in 1690.
examples.note: site = the piece of ground where something was or will be built

examples.text: The cathedral is an **imposing** 19th-century building in the French Gothic style.
Neither market **caters specifically for** tourists, but anyone who enjoys a real working market will appreciate their charm.
The Crawford Art Gallery is **well worth a visit**. It regularly **puts on** adventurous **exhibitions** by contemporary artists.
The town centre **tends to be** very crowded on Saturdays.

lesson.heading: Facilities
rows: swimming pool, sports centre, golf course, tennis courts, football pitch, skating rink
theatre, opera house, concert hall, radio station, art gallery
school, college, university, library, adult education centre, museum
restaurant, take-away, hotel, B&B (bed and breakfast), youth hostel, club
bus service, taxi rank, car hire, car park, parking meters
health centre, law courts, registry office, citizens' advice bureau, job centre, department store, chemist's, garden centre, police station, Town/City Hall
estate agent, housing estate, industrial estate

lesson.heading: Problems in cities
rows: traffic very slow; commuters get very stressed
too much traffic, especially in the rush hour
poverty - people have no money to spend on housing
too many people living in one place

lesson.heading: Adjectives to describe a city
rows: important in history, with old buildings
with no one on the streets, e.g. at night

lesson.text: Say **open spaces**, not ~~open places~~: *There are a lot of open spaces in the centre of London.*

exercises.prompt: Where would you go in order to do each of these things?
We didn't feel like cooking, so we bought a meal to eat at home from the Chinese ___.
exercises.explanation: A take-away sells cooked food to eat somewhere else.

exercises.prompt: Most of the main hotels are within walking ___ of the centre.
exercises.explanation: *Within walking distance* means close enough to walk to.

exercises.prompt: An interesting new Science Park has been built on the ___ of the town, about two kilometres from the city centre.
exercises.explanation: The outskirts are the outer parts of a town, away from the centre.

exercises.prompt: Cambridge has a ___ of around 108,900, many of whom are students.
exercises.explanation: A town's population is the number of people who live in it.

exercises.prompt: A number of the old university buildings are built on the ___ of former monasteries.
exercises.explanation: A site is the piece of ground where a building stands or once stood.

exercises.prompt: Most of the more picturesque colleges ___ the River Cam.
exercises.explanation: If a building overlooks something, it has a view over it from above.

exercises.prompt: The Fitzwilliam Museum is well ___ visiting.
exercises.explanation: *Well worth + -ing* means it is definitely a good idea.

exercises.prompt: Which city problem does each suggested solution deal with?

pairs.left: They should provide good-quality state housing.
There should be stricter laws about traffic emissions.
They should restrict the number of people living in any one area.
People who destroy public property should do community service.
We need a much better public transport system.

exercises.prompt: Would each adjective please a tourist or put them off?

options: There are a lot of open spaces in the centre of London.
There are a lot of open places in the centre of London.
There are a lot of opened spaces in the centre of London.
There are a lot of open sites in the centre of London.
exercises.explanation: The fixed phrase is *open spaces*, never *open places*.

exercises.statement: A city is generally larger than a town and has a wider range of facilities.
exercises.explanation: Correct - the words overlap, but *city* suggests size and a fuller range of facilities.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to describe an art gallery.
exercises.answer: It regularly puts on adventurous exhibitions by contemporary artists.
exercises.explanation: A gallery or theatre *puts on* an exhibition or a show.
